Thus, it is important to identify mitigation strategies and install more efficient components in the HP-TES to minimize the required recharge energy and avoid creating a secondary artificial peak. As a first step, the single-speed pump in the secondary loop was replaced with a variable-speed pump in Modelica (Figure 42). The variable-speed pump was modeled using pump affinity laws, and a PI controller was used to control the pump speed (i.e., the heat transfer from the plate heat exchanger to the thermal battery). As compressor power is dominant, at lower outdoor temperatures, the compressor efficiency is highest, as lower cycle temperatures are achieved and heat can be more easily rejected to a colder heat sink. The variable-speed pump enhances the recharge by maximizing the water-side heat transfer in the thermal battery. At higher outdoor temperatures, the variable-speed pump's effects are minimal, as the compressor efficiency begins to degrade due to higher temperature lifts required, and the outdoor heat exchanger's heat transfer effectiveness decreases. In Honolulu, HI, nighttime temperatures range from 14 – 20°C, corresponding to reductions in recharge energy of 10 – 33%. This shows there is potential to use this system in Honolulu, HI, without creating a nighttime peak during recharge, keeping the recharge energy close to the discharge energy. Nonetheless, additional mitigation through further component improvements and optimal control strategies is required to maximize cost savings and achieve some energy savings in this location. Unlike Riverside, CA, this location has a more extended peak utility hour period— summer: 12–9 PM; winter: 6–10 AM & 6–10 PM [98]. The prototype small office commercial building operates from 6 AM to 8 PM [75]. The extended peak period provides greater flexibility to align the TES discharge for the most efficient operation: discharge from 12 – 2 PM in cooling mode (i.e., the hottest time of day) and from 7 – 9 AM in heating mode (i.e., the coldest time of day). Assessing monthly annual consumption in Tampa, FL, it was found that heating-mode savings are limited to December, January, and February (Figure 44).
